Reframed with insights from the monetary economics literature: The statement is candid about severe pandemic-driven hardship and elevated uncertainty (consistent with evidence that COVID-19 raised economic policy uncertainty and combined supply–demand shocks), but it pairs that with a strong commitment to accommodative policy at the zero lower bound. The FOMC’s zero-to-0.25% rate, balance-sheet expansion in Treasuries and agency MBS (QE), and explicit forward guidance align with research showing these tools lower term premia, support credit flows, and help stabilize inflation expectations when conventional policy is constrained. The shift to average-inflation targeting—a “makeup” strategy flagged by Powell in 2020—matches theory emphasizing the Taylor principle and credible commitments to allow inflation to run moderately above target to re-anchor expectations. Net tone: cautious due to pandemic risks, but materially supported by credible, literature-backed policy tools.
